1). This unit consists of discontinuous gray sandstone and siltstone with occasional shale layers and a coal bed (referred to as Stray 1 coal) which is 15 to 75 feet above the Rosebud-McKay coal. The overburden unit is present in most of Tract III, but only in part of Tract II. There, the upper sandstones and siltstones have largely been removed by erosion and the unit is represented by clinker (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1, p.30). This unit is also represented by clinker on the western and northern parts of Tract III. The clinker, where exposed, has a moderate to high infiltration rate.
The sandstones and siltstones that form the overburden in Tract III are weathered and uncemented to a depth of 20 to 50 feet below land surface, and have moderate porosity and infiltration capacity. Fractures in the overburden are rare except in the Stray 1 coal. The siltstones and sandstones have intergranular porosity, whereas the porosity of the Stray 1 coal results from fractures.
The overburden is up to 100 feet thick on the eastern part of Tract

III. It is 300 feet thick in the southeast part of the Tract, which is

the only place in the project area where the unit is an aquifer. Throughout the rest of the project area, the overburden unit is above the water

table. It does transmit recharge to underlying aquifers.
